summary: Oxygen, iron, silicon and aluminium are gettable, but carbon (#17), nitrogen (#34) and gold (#75) are the classic wrong guesses, each showing its ppm.
reasons: Builder's own replays, pending a real judge (the builder knew the answers when writing them). A casual order found 7.

CRC figures for the continental crust, 94 elements. The ten trace elements whose figures are powers of ten (xenon, radium, polonium...) and plutonium and neptunium are answers that read "a trace, under 0.0001 ppm"; the table's text loses their exponents. Lab-made elements are free.
Figures show as ppm (461,000 ppm for oxygen); the share in percent would read easier but isn't a column of its own.
